stories.title: Biltmore Championship Round 3 — Shipley Leads at -15, Kohles One Back

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text: Neal Shipley (-15) leads the Biltmore Championship by one over Ben Kohles (-14) after a career-low 62 on Friday. Round 3 is live today at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove. NBC at noon ET.

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: Shipley. Kohles. Castillo. Greyserman. Four players within four shots heading into Saturday at the Biltmore Championship. Final round is Sunday. This one is far from over.

facebook.long_form:
Neal Shipley posted a career-low 62 on Friday to take the 36-hole lead at the Biltmore Championship at -15 — one shot ahead of Ben Kohles.

Four players are within four shots of the lead heading into Round 3 today. Ricky Castillo and Max Greyserman sit at -11. This is as tight as it gets at a PGA Tour event.

Shipley, Kohles, and Castillo tee off together Saturday morning. NBC picks up coverage at noon ET, Golf Channel takes over at 12:30 PM. Final round is Sunday.

This is also the first PGA Tour event in western North Carolina in 84 years. The Cliffs at Walnut Cove is putting on a show.

Who wins the Biltmore Championship? 👇

facebook.long_form:
Five days from now, the 2026 Presidents Cup gets underway at Medinah Country Club.

Practice rounds start Tuesday. Competition begins Thursday, September 24 with five four-ball matches. Friday brings five foursomes. Saturday features four four-ball in the morning and four foursomes in the afternoon. Sunday closes with 12 singles.

USA Captain Brandt Snedeker vs. International Captain Geoff Ogilvy. The USA goes in with a 13-1-1 all-time record in this event.

USA team: Scheffler, Young, Clark, Henley, Burns, Morikawa (automatics) + Gotterup, Schauffele, Thomas, Cantlay, Bridgeman, Koivun (captain's picks).

stories.title: LIV Golf Bankruptcy — 24 Days to Oct. 13 Player Commitment Deadline

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: 24 days to LIV Golf's October 13 player commitment deadline. Under the BC Partners deal, players would own 52.5% of a restructured LIV. The clock is running and Rahm still hasn't said yes.

x_posts.label: Post 6
x_posts.text: PIF is out. BC Partners is in. Players own 52.5% under LIV's restructuring plan. But they need 2/3 of player claims — by dollar amount — to commit by October 13. That math runs through Rahm.

facebook.long_form:
LIV Golf's restructuring deadline is 24 days away — October 13.

Here's what has to happen: players holding at least 2/3 of total claim dollar amounts AND at least 1/2 by headcount must commit to LIV 2.0 under the BC Partners deal. The deal offers players 52.5% ownership of the restructured tour. PIF exits entirely.

The math runs through the top creditors. Jon Rahm is owed $7.47 million — the largest individual player claim. Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson are also major creditors. Their collective decision carries enormous weight.

Rahm has been publicly noncommittal. He reached an agreement with the DP World Tour in May, paid his outstanding fines, and said this week he sees "opportunity" there. That language matters.

If the threshold isn't met by October 13, the BC Partners deal is likely off. LIV 2.0 doesn't happen. And the tour that spent $4+ billion Saudi dollars on golf restructuring ends in bankruptcy liquidation.

24 days.

---
